name: NotePlan
subcategory: daily notes, tasks and calendar in markdown
tagline: A Mac and iOS app that merges daily markdown notes, tasks and your calendar into one timeline.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The data model here is not a secret: plain markdown files, one per day, with checkbox tasks and a calendar rendered next to them. An agent can build a local daily-note app with task rollover, backlinks and a read-only calendar feed in a weekend, and because the files are yours you can keep them in git or Obsidian forever. What breaks is everything Apple-shaped: native Mac and iPhone apps, iCloud sync that actually works offline, two-way Apple Calendar and Reminders sync, and the timeblocking flow that makes NotePlan feel like one surface instead of three panes. You can read an ICS feed easily, but writing events back to a calendar you sync elsewhere is where the weekend ends. Build it if you live on one machine, pay if you want the same view on your phone in a meeting.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app over a folder of markdown daily notes with checkbox tasks, unfinished-task rollover, wiki links and a read-only calendar column from an ICS feed.
requirements: A local folder for markdown notes, optionally in iCloud Drive or a git repo
An ICS subscription URL if you want calendar events shown
No accounts, no server, runs on localhost
whatYouLose: Native Mac, iPhone and iPad apps with offline sync between them
Two-way Apple Calendar and Reminders integration, including creating events from tasks
Timeblocking that drags a task onto the calendar and keeps both in sync
Themes, templates, plugins and the small polish of years of iteration
Fast global search and a shortcut-driven UI you do not have to design yourself
moatNotes: The lock-in is not the file format, it is deliberately open. It is the Apple ecosystem plumbing and the muscle memory.
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay for NotePlan because the same notes need to be on a laptop at a desk and a phone in a hallway, and because it talks to the calendar and reminders they already use rather than asking them to migrate. A localhost app cannot do either of those without becoming a real sync project with a mobile client, which is a different scale of work. The markdown-on-disk promise also means the paid version is a low-risk bet: if the company disappears, the notes are still readable, which removes the usual reason to self-host in the first place.
notes: The DIY build is genuinely pleasant on a desktop and genuinely useless the moment you stand up and walk away from it.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user daily notes and tasks app called Timeline. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Node 20, TypeScript, Fastify backend
- React + Vite frontend, plain CSS, no component library
- Markdown files on disk as the only storage. No database.
- chokidar to watch the notes folder, ws for live reload of changed files

Data model:
- NOTES_DIR from .env, default ./notes
- Daily notes at notes/daily/YYYY-MM-DD.md, project notes anywhere under notes/
- Tasks are markdown checkboxes: "* [ ] thing" open, "* [x] thing" done, "* [-] thing" cancelled
- Support inline tags (#tag), wiki links ([[Note Title]]) and @mentions, parsed with a small regex layer, no plugin system

Features, in scope:
- Three-pane layout: date sidebar with a month calendar, the selected day's note in a markdown editor, and a right column showing calendar events for that day
- Editor: CodeMirror 6 with markdown mode, click a checkbox in the rendered gutter to toggle it and write the file immediately, debounced 300ms save
- Rollover: a button and an on-first-open-of-today action that moves unfinished tasks from the most recent previous daily note into today, leaving a "moved" marker behind
- Backlinks panel listing every file containing [[Current Note]]
- Global search across all files with ripgrep-style substring matching, plain JS is fine
- Read-only calendar column: fetch ICS_URL from .env, parse with ical.js, cache to disk, show events with times for the selected day. If ICS_URL is missing, show an empty state, do not crash.
- Keyboard: cmd+k search, cmd+t jump to today, cmd+enter toggle task under cursor

Out of scope, do not build: mobile app, sync, writing to any calendar, Apple Reminders, sharing, themes, plugins, AI features.

Deliver: npm install then npm run dev serves the app at localhost:5173 with the API on 3001. Include .env.example with NOTES_DIR and ICS_URL, a README with a five-line quickstart, and seed the notes folder with three example daily notes so the UI is not empty on first run.
